items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish. Chars voices two funny cartoon characters (a smug gold bar and a nervous banknote), short and punchy, performed exactly as described in each bracket.
lines: Narrator
One king's trip to Cairo made gold cheaper for twelve years. How do you make gold lose value?
Narrator
In thirteen twenty-four, Mansa Musa, ruler of Mali, stopped there on his way to Mecca.
Narrator
The story goes his caravan carried tons of gold.
Chars
[smug, deep, rich gold bar, very pleased with himself] Finally, a man who understood me.
Narrator
So how did one man do that?
Narrator
He gave it away. To officials, to emirs, to the treasury. His people spent it everywhere.
Narrator
Suddenly, Cairo had more gold than it knew what to do with.
Narrator
And then things got really strange.
Narrator
A gold coin worth twenty-five silver coins fell to twenty-two, or less.
Narrator
A Cairo writer said it stayed low for about twelve years.
Narrator
That's the mirage: gold isn't valuable for being gold. It's valuable for being rare.
Chars
[delighted, squeaky banknote, surprised to be winning] So I'm rare too?
Narrator
Flood a city with it, and even a king's gold becomes ordinary.
Narrator
Comment: what would you do with a ton of gold?
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
